item.title: wctr-relay commands
item.description:
wctr-relay is one binary: serve runs the relay; every other command is a client of its control API. Locally they use the state directory’s admin socket (0600: its permissions are the credential); for a remote relay, --server URL --token-file FILE [--ca-file ROOT.pem], where URL is the relay’s --admin-listen address over https (the token is never a flag value). --state-dir (default <user config dir>/wctr-relay) applies to all.

Command What
init [--name N] [--ip A] create the state directory (0700): admin token, session-token signing keys, and the internal CA for those names and addresses
serve run the relay
class create NAME a class; flags --cidr (default 10.42.0.0/16), --session-bits (24), --domain (class), --template isolated|neutron, --allow sub:…|email:…|group:…, --require-identity
class list classes and their join codes
class sessions CLASS sessions: label, name, subnet, connected
class kick CLASS SESSION end a session: its connection, ports and tokens
class rotate-code CLASS a new join code; the old one stops admitting
class delete CLASS delete the class and what the relay knows of its students
sg list --class C groups and their rules
sg create NAME --class C [--stateless] [--description D] an empty group (it allows nothing)
sg delete GROUP --class C a group no port uses
rule add GROUP --class C --ingress|--egress [--proto tcp|udp|icmp|any] [--port 80|8000-8080] [--remote-ip PREFIX|--remote-group G] allow a flow
rule delete RULE --class C remove a rule; the flows only it allowed are reset
port list --class C [--student S] ports: name, address, groups
port set PORT --class C [--sg a,b] [--port-security on|off] a port’s groups (replaces the list)
flows --class C [--follow] [--deny-only] [--student S] [--backlog N] the flow log
explain --class C SRC DST PROTO/PORT what the firewall would decide, and which rules
ca export, ca fingerprint, ca rotate [--name] [--ip] the internal CA
teacher-session --class C --out FILE a session token (written 0600) for the teacher’s own containers
flowmap --class C --url URL (the relay’s https address) the link to the class’s live flow map, with a read-only 12-hour ticket in its fragment (v0.2.0)
version the version

A port is named by its id, its DNS name (web.alice.class) or student/container (alice/web).

serve flags

Flag Default What
--listen :8443 the address students reach (data plane /v1/data, join, /v1/info)
--tls internal internal, files, acme, or off (loopback only)
--cert, --key PEM files for --tls files, re-read when they change
--acme-domain, --acme-email, --acme-directory, --acme-cache ACME for --tls acme (default CA: Let’s Encrypt)
--eab-kid, --eab-hmac-file External Account Binding (the HMAC key in a 0600 file)
--acme-http also answer http-01 on this address (e.g. :80)
--origin go-wasmcontainers.github.io other origins allowed to open the data channel
--host Host names served; any other is refused
--oidc-issuer, --oidc-audience, --oidc-type OpenID Connect token verification
--teacher-group groups-claim value granting the teacher role on --admin-listen
--admin-listen also serve the admin API on this address (TLS)
--session-ttl 12h session token lifetime
--audit-retention 720h how long the audit log keeps events
--relay-id host name this relay’s id

item.title: The live flow map
item.description:
Since relay v0.2.0.

wctr-relay flowmap --class <class> --url <the relay's https address>

prints a link; open it on the projector. Each student is a box holding their containers, coloured by security group. Each flow is a line between two containers whose width follows its throughput. A refused flow is a dashed red line, and the event log beside the map says which rule was missing (“no ingress rule of … allows it”). Click a container for its address and groups, or a flow for its counters and the rules that allowed it; the arrow keys move from container to container. The filter box dims everything that does not match a student, a container or a group.

Who can see what

Viewer Credential Sees
The teacher the link from wctr-relay flowmap: a read-only ticket in the URL fragment (never sent to a server, removed from the address bar when the page loads), valid 12 hours the whole class
A student their own session token (#class=…&session=…) only the flows that touch their own containers, and the containers at the other end

The ticket allows watching that class’s map and nothing else: it cannot change a rule, list the groups, or join the class.

How it works

The relay aggregates its flow log per edge — source container, destination container, protocol and port — and streams one update per tick (4 per second) over FlowLogService.WatchFlowMap, a server stream of the Connect protocol. A slow page gets the newest map, never a backlog. An update holds at most 400 containers, 2 000 flows and 200 events.

The page is a Go WebAssembly application built on go-widgets’ GraphView (a node-link graph over a view model, added to go-widgets for this page and reusable elsewhere) and LogView. The relay serves it itself, under a strict Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' — no inline script, nothing loaded from anywhere else, so it works on a classroom LAN with no internet.

Getting a binary that has it

The page’s WebAssembly is about 5 MB, so it is not in the repository: the binaries attached to each release carry it. From source:

go run ./internal/buildflowmap
go install -tags flowmap ./cmd/wctr-relay

A plain go install …@latest serves the page, which then says the map is missing from that build.

Not yet

Pause and replay of the last minutes; the relay keeps the last 1 000 events, the page shows the last 200.

item.title: Relay
item.description:
wctr-relay connects the WASI containers of a class’s browsers (or engines) through one relay that is also a firewall, with security groups modelled on OpenStack Neutron. It runs on the teacher’s laptop for a classroom LAN, or on a server for remote students with OpenID Connect sign-in. Release v0.2.0 of go-wasmcontainers/relay covers milestones M-relay-1, M-relay-2 and M-relay-2b (the live flow map) of the design.

What works today: the relay, its firewall, its control API, the wctr-relay command and the live flow map, tested natively and, for the flow map, in Chromium and Firefox. The engine does not use the relay yet (its network driver is being written), so containers in the playground cannot reach each other through it yet.

Install

Download the binary for your system from the releases (it includes the flow map), or build it:

go install github.com/go-wasmcontainers/relay/cmd/wctr-relay@v0.2.0 # without the flow map page

Pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0; Linux, macOS and Windows.

Start a class (teacher) 

wctr-relay init --name relay.local --ip 192.168.1.10 # state directory, admin token, internal CA
wctr-relay serve --listen :8443 &
wctr-relay class create "Networking 101" # prints the class id and the join code

Students join with the code. Each gets a subnet (10.42.<n>.0/24), each container an address and the name <container>.<student>.class. A new class starts isolated: no ingress, egress to the teacher’s subnet only. Opening flows is the lab:

wctr-relay sg create web --class <class>
wctr-relay rule add web --class <class> --ingress --proto tcp --port 80
wctr-relay rule add default --class <class> --egress --proto tcp --port 80
wctr-relay port set alice/web --class <class> --sg default,web
wctr-relay flows --class <class> --follow # every allow and deny, with the rule that decided
wctr-relay explain --class <class> bob/curl alice/web tcp/80

Deleting a rule resets, at once, the flows only that rule allowed.

Certificates

Students’ browsers must trust the relay’s certificate. In order of preference:

  1. a publicly trusted certificate for a name the school owns: --tls acme --acme-domain class.example-school.fr (ACME through go-authn/servercert), or --tls files --cert … --key …;
  2. the relay’s internal CA (the default, --tls internal): install the root printed by wctr-relay ca export on the class’s machines; it is name-constrained to the relay’s names and addresses;
  3. behind Caddy or another TLS proxy: --tls off --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 (refused on any other address).

  • Command reference
  • The live flow map
  • Security model

item.title: Relay security model
item.description:
Principals

Who Credential Where May
Teacher, on the relay’s machine the admin socket (0600 in a 0700 state directory) Unix socket everything
Teacher, remote the admin token (Authorization: Bearer) or an OpenID Connect token carrying --teacher-group --admin-listen only, over TLS everything
Student a session token from Join (join code, plus an OpenID Connect identity when the class requires one) --listen their own ports and flow decisions; read the groups

The public listener never grants the teacher role, whatever arrives on it (the admin token included).

What the relay refuses

  • Identity is the relay’s: it assigns every address and port; a frame that names a port the session does not own is refused, a datagram from a source port the sender has not bound is dropped.
  • Authentication before the upgrade: the session token is a WebSocket subprotocol (bearer.<token>), checked before the upgrade and before any per-session state; it never appears in a URL. Unknown Origin and Host are refused.
  • Pre-authentication limits per source address on joins and upgrades, a cap on concurrent handshakes, header timeouts and sizes.
  • Bounds: 16 KiB frames, 64 KiB stream windows, and per session: 256 streams, 64 listeners, 10 ports, 32 pending connects, 2 MiB/s and 2 000 frames/s; a connection whose send queue passes 4 MiB is closed. Per class: 50 security groups and 500 rules (Neutron’s quotas).
  • A frame that does not decode, data beyond the window, or a frame out of place closes the connection.
  • Tokens: Ed25519, one fixed layout and one algorithm, checked against the relay’s clock; a kicked session’s tokens stop working at once.

Secrets

The admin token, the signing keys, the CA key, an EAB key and the state file are 0600 files of the relay’s user, refused if anyone else can read them, never on a command line, in an environment variable or in a URL. The internal CA is name-constrained: even its key cannot sign for another site.

What the relay keeps about students

Per session: the display name typed, a derived DNS label, and — with OpenID Connect — a pseudonymous hash of issuer and subject (never the token, the e-mail address or the groups, which are checked at join time and dropped). Flow logs hold addresses and ports, not contents. Deleting a class deletes all of it; the audit log (logins, refusals, kicks, rule changes) keeps 30 days by default. The teacher’s institution is the controller under the GDPR.

Tested

Every point above has a test in the repository; the decoders of untrusted input (frames, tokens, join codes, labels, rule specifications, and the relay fed arbitrary frames) are fuzzed in CI, and govulncheck runs on every change.
